newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Ireland will enter EMU on time if qualifies - Ahern.
newsitem.headline: Ireland will enter EMU on time if qualifies - Ahern.

text.p: A spokesman for Ireland's newly-elected government on Wednesday denied reports and market talk that it would delay entry into EMU.
"There has been no change in our stance. Bertie Ahern has said and still maintains that Ireland will enter EMU at the start date if we qualify," a spokesman for Ahern told Reuters.
He was reponding to market talk and a newspaper report saying that Ahern, who won elections at the weekend, had hinted at a possible delay in Ireland's EMU membership.
The Irish pound breached 2.60 marks and moved up towards 0.93 stg on talk that Ahern, the Prime Minister-elect, had cast doubts on Ireland's entry date on a radio talk show on Tuesday evening.
"Bertie Ahern has contributed to the strength of the punt this morning with comments in the media hinting at doubts about when Ireland will enter EMU," one currency dealer said.

The dealer said there were "a lot of short positions in the punt out there on the assumption that Ireland would enter EMU on time and that it would enter a single currency at its central parity rate of 2.41 marks within the European Exchange Rate mechanism."
By 0939 GMT the Irish pound was trading at 0.9270/00 stg and 2.6043/58 marks.

Ahern told RTE radio that if Britain was not going to go in for the long term "it would put a lot of pressures on us which we would need to think long and hard about", a newspaper report quoted Ahern as saying.
The new Fianna Fail/Progressive Democrat alliance, which polled two seats short of a majority at the poll, is expected to have a new government in place by the weekend.
Ahern will be formally voted in as prime minister when parliament reconvenes on June 26.
The defeated centre-left 'Rainbow Coalition' of Prime Minister John Bruton will form a caretaker administration until then.
